content: •, 6h￼, TRADERS: Something weird is happening in this earnings season that you need to know about., Companies are beating earnings expectations... and their stocks are FALLING. Let me break down what Charles Schwab's senior investment strategist just revealed: Companies beating EPS forecasts are underperforming the S&P 500 by 0.35% after reporting. This is the WORST spread we've seen since Q4 2020. Think about that. You do everything right as a company. Beat analyst expectations. Deliver solid numbers. And the market says "thanks, but no thanks" and sells off your stock anyway. Real examples from this week: Blackstone - Beat on top AND bottom line. Stock dropped Thursday. Coca-Cola - Posted a strong double-beat. Faded Wednesday. So what's really going on here? Three things I'm watching: Expectations were already sky-high going into earnings season. Good news was priced in before companies even reported. Investors are more worried about forward guidance than backward results. Q4 outlooks are introducing caution. We might be entering a new phase where solid earnings alone aren't enough. The market wants proof of SUSTAINED growth, not just one good quarter. Here's the big question for you: If beating earnings doesn't move stocks higher anymore, what's your strategy for trading through earnings season? Are you still playing earnings? Avoiding them completely? Or waiting for the post-report selloff to buy the dip? Drop your strategy below. I want to hear how you're navigating this. And if you've been burned by an earnings beat that tanked anyway, you're not alone. Comment which stock got you and let's compare notes, 13, 19
